A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the critical zone C Q relation is controlled by the permeability architecture of hillslope, and is a function of flow rate, mineral dissolution kinetics, and the degree of mineral saturation.

for minerals with low CeqRmax, the concentration in stream is more dependent on the flow rate and Ks distribution, whereas for minerals with higher CeqRmax the concentration in stream becomes more dependent on the groundwater age.
the C Q relation in the stream reflects the balance between the transport and reaction controlled mechanisms in the critical zone.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the critical zone is not a passive reactor for weathering reactions, and that flow path heterogeneity in the critical zone is a critical control on the spatiotemopral pattern of weathering and the resulting stream C Q relation
the C Q relation is not a simple function of Ks, but is also a function of the intrinsic weathering rate and equilibrium concentration of the mineral.
the C Q relation and concentration in the stream are controlled by both the flow dynamics and the intrinsic weathering kinetics.
